answer: A clone needs a document. At join the client taps the passport's NFC chip, reads the signed security object and follows the chain to the issuing state's root. The registry hashes number, birth date and nationality, so one book seats one key, from a tundra village to a city desk. Chip keys never export, and a relay still needs a body at the reader. Real books trade near 900 dollars, so fifty clones run 45,000 dollars plus fifty holders. The zenith of that budget buys nothing lasting, since each holder can walk off with the ferrous key. A seal holds because one state pressed the original.
